market_specific_notes: Newark sits inside one of the densest civil surgeon markets in the country, and the New York metropolitan area does not respect state lines. A ZIP search on the federal locator will return offices across the river; a search by city name will not. Decide how far you are prepared to travel twice before you narrow the list.

USCIS recognises all state and local health departments as civil surgeons for one specific purpose — completing “the vaccination assessments for refugees seeking adjustment of status”. In Newark that body is the Newark Department of Health & Community Wellness. It covers vaccinations for that category, not the full examination for everyone.

USCIS also warns that “Many health insurance plans do not cover all portions of this examination.” Bring the card, then ask whether the practice accepts the plan for immigration medical examinations specifically.

Do not confuse the two places. The immigration medical examination is done by a civil surgeon in a private practice. The USCIS field office is where, in its own words, it holds “Interviews for all non-asylum cases (for example, getting a Green Card)” and “Naturalization ceremonies”. Newark's is in the Peter Rodino Federal Building at 970 Broad Street. If the civil surgeon you choose is across the river, that is a separate journey again — worth weighing before you book on price alone.
Use the checklist below before you decide how far to travel. Crossing a state line is not the obstacle it looks like; a second visit is.
local_vetting_points: Search uscis.gov/tools/find-a-civil-surgeon by ZIP code and widen the radius deliberately, since the nearest designated office may not be in New Jersey.
Confirm the practice appears in the federal locator under the name it bills and answers the phone under.
Ask whether tuberculosis testing is done on site and what a positive result does to the price and the timeline.
Ask what the office does when a vaccination record cannot be produced.
Ask who signs the completed form and how long after the visit.
typical_cost_ranges: USCIS publishes no price and says why: “Fees for immigration medical examinations are established by the civil surgeon. Fees may vary by civil surgeon.” There is no New Jersey rate and no metropolitan rate.
Because the search radius crosses a state line, you will often be comparing quotes from two states. USCIS's advice still holds: call several offices, because the cost “can vary significantly”.
Ask each office for five separate figures — examination, tuberculosis and syphilis testing, missing vaccines, completing and sealing the form, follow-up visit — before you let travel distance decide.
Filing Form I-693 costs $0. The published fee attached to the case is the I-485: paper $1,440 or online $1,390 for an applicant over 14.
payment_options: USCIS tells applicants to confirm acceptable forms of payment with the office in advance — worth doing on the same call as the price question.
Ask whether a deposit holds the appointment, and whether it is applied to a second visit if one is needed.
wait_time_notes: Weigh the second visit before you choose on distance. An office twenty minutes further away that finishes the form in one visit can be the faster option overall.
Ask how long after the examination the signed form is usually ready when records are complete and nothing is missing.
availability_notes: Confirm whether a same-week appointment refers to the examination or to the completed paperwork.
If a filing deadline is close, name the date on the call and ask the office to commit or decline.
named_resources_or_providers: USCIS Find a Civil Surgeon locator (official) — uscis.gov/tools/find-a-civil-surgeon
Newark Department of Health & Community Wellness — newarknj.gov/169/Health-Community-Wellness. USCIS recognises local health departments as civil surgeons for the refugee vaccination assessment.
USCIS Newark field office (NEW) — Peter Rodino Federal Building, 970 Broad Street, Newark, NJ 07102. From the USCIS field office ZIP data file at uscis.gov/about-us/find-a-uscis-office/field-offices.

New Jersey Immunization Information System (NJIIS) — nj.gov/health/vaccines/. The state page says: “New Jersey residents can view their official immunization records online through the free Docket app or myHealthNJ.com.” Both destinations are private services rather than government sites.
New Jersey Department of Health, Tuberculosis Control Program — nj.gov/health/hivstdtb/tb/.
USCIS Form I-693 page — uscis.gov/i-693, for the current form edition and filing instructions.
Listings are neutral examples and starting points for your own verification. Nothing here is a ranking or an endorsement.
city_intro_override: Newark residents searching for a civil surgeon are searching a two-state market. The official USCIS locator takes a ZIP code and a radius, and that is the search that reflects where you can actually get to on a weekday. Verify designation there before you compare price, language or speed.

primary_city_decision_block.title: Local civil surgeon comparison checklist
items: Verify designation in the official USCIS locator before comparing anything else.
Ask for the price broken into examination, labs, vaccines, form completion and follow-up.
Gather the vaccination records USCIS names before the first visit.
Ask what a positive tuberculosis test would do to the cost and the schedule.
Tell the office whether the I-485 is going by mail or online.
Confirm the form edition and the date the civil surgeon intends to sign.

heading: Newark: a two-state search area, and one federal record of who is designated
i693_document_requirements: Form I-693 in the edition USCIS currently accepts.

Government-issued photo identification such as a valid passport or driver's licence. For an applicant aged 14 or younger, USCIS accepts identification showing name, date and place of birth and a parent's full name — a birth certificate with an English translation, or an affidavit.

A record of your vaccinations or immunisations, covering what USCIS names: DT, DTP, DTaP, Td, Tdap, OPV, IPV, MMR, Hib, Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B, Varicella, Pneumococcal, Influenza, Rotavirus and Meningococcal disease.
Your health insurance card, with the coverage question already prepared.
Payment, in a form the office has told you it accepts.
vaccination_handling_notes: The records are the cheapest part of this process to get right and the most expensive to get wrong.

New Jersey's registry is NJIIS, and the state routes residents to it through the Docket app or myHealthNJ.com. Both are private services, so read what you are agreeing to before you enter identifying details.
If you were vaccinated in New York rather than New Jersey, the record is in a different system entirely and you will need to request it there.
New Jersey operates a statewide immunisation information system through which residents can request their own record; ask the clinic which record format it will accept before you order anything.
Refugees adjusting status may complete the vaccination assessment at a state or local health department under the USCIS blanket designation described above.
bilingual_support: The federal locator carries a Languages Spoken filter listing well over a hundred named languages — an entry the practice made with USCIS, which is a stronger signal than a claim on a clinic's own site.
A language listed in the tool tells you it exists in the practice. Ask separately whether it covers the paperwork review, which is where a misunderstanding becomes a correction.
appointment_booking_notes: Decide before the exam how the I-485 is being filed. By mail the envelope stays sealed. Online, USCIS instructs you to open it and upload the form, then keep the original and the envelope until the case is decided.
Confirm the form edition and the intended signing date. Only the 01/20/25 edition is accepted for signatures dated 3 July 2025 or later.
Ask whether the slot you are offered is intake, examination, or the full path to a signed form.

Ask when the sealed packet is ready and what happens if a correction is needed after you have travelled home. If the office is across a state line, a correction that requires a return visit is a much bigger problem than it sounds.
